Maintaining the target range at 5.25–5.5% and continuing balance‑sheet runoff while noting that “risks … are moving into better balance” is consistent with a Taylor‑rule/DSGE policy framework that prioritizes anchoring expected inflation (references to Taylor rule and DSGE usage). The emphasis on “greater confidence” before cutting aligns with inflation‑forecast targeting in the literature (Svensson; Svensson and Woodford), which helps counter the classic inflationary bias under discretion and supports credibility. With job gains strong and unemployment low—conditions close to the natural rate—the New Keynesian Phillips Curve and evidence of inflation persistence under Calvo‑style pricing (Gali–Gertler; Calvo) suggest disinflation can require a sustained restrictive stance, justifying a hold. Ongoing QT in Treasuries and agency MBS tightens financial conditions in line with research linking monetary aggregates/asset supplies to inflation dynamics and term premia. Overall tone: cautiously constructive—real activity is resilient and the risk balance improved—but still constrained by persistent inflation risks and the need to preserve anchored expectations.
